instructions:
### ROLE ###
You maintain a small, growing set of CONCEPT SCHEMES (entity categories) for a knowledge registry built from cybersecurity incident reports. A group of entities extracted from several reports has just been found to be close to each other and far from every existing scheme. Decide whether the group is a genuinely new scheme or an alias of an existing one, and name it.

### EXISTING SCHEMES ###
- Vulnerability: A flaw or weakness in software, hardware, or a system that can be exploited to compromise security.
- Software Product: A program, application, operating system, or software component designed for end users or computing systems.
- Technology Vendor: A company or organization that develops, manufactures, or supplies software, hardware, or technology services.
- Country: A sovereign nation, state, or distinct territorial body with its own government.
- Government Agency: An official institution, ministry, department, or administrative body operating under the authority of a national or regional government.

### THE GROUP ###
Each line is one entity with the description written at extraction time:
- Petya [malware] — A family of encrypting ransomware targeting Microsoft Windows-based systems.
- Misha [malware] — A ransomware strain often distributed alongside or as a fallback for Petya ransomware.
- major[.]exe [malware] — A malicious executable file downloaded following exploitation of CVE-2017-11882.
- AZORult [malware] — An information-stealing Trojan malware designed to collect browser credentials, cookies, and sensitive user information from infected systems.
- CoronaMap.exe [malware] — A malicious executable disguised as a coronavirus tracking application that executes the AZORult trojan in the background.
- Corona-virus-Map.com.exe [malware] — A malicious executable file used to deliver information-stealing malware under the guise of a coronavirus map.

### RULES ###
- A scheme is a KIND of entity (e.g. "Hacker group", "Malware family", "Software product", "Government body", "Internet domain", "Country"), never a role in an incident and never a single entity.
- Return `"verdict": "alias-of"` with `"target"` set to an existing scheme's label when the group is the same kind as that scheme (different wording, same meaning). Judge by MEANING of the descriptions, not by surface words.
- Return `"verdict": "new"` when no existing scheme covers the group. Then give:
  - `prefLabel`: a short English noun phrase, 1–3 words, singular, Title Case (e.g. "Malware Family").
  - `definition`: one sentence, at most 25 words, stating what belongs to the scheme, general enough to hold across reports.
  - `altLabels`: 0–3 alternative English labels.
- If the group mixes clearly different kinds, name the kind of the MAJORITY and list the minority entity names in `outliers`.
- If uncertain between alias and new, prefer `new`: an extra scheme can be merged later; a wrong merge cannot be undone cheaply.

### OUTPUT ###
A single raw JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary:
{ "verdict": "new" | "alias-of", "target": "<existing label or null>", "prefLabel": "...", "definition": "...", "altLabels": [...], "outliers": [...] }
text: Decide and name the group now.
response: {"verdict": "new", "target": null, "prefLabel": "Malware", "definition": "Software, code, or executable files intentionally designed to disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.", "altLabels": ["Malicious Software", "Malware Family", "Malware Strain"], "outliers": []}
